Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Private VPC — post-call recap and proposed next tests

Hi Sam — great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through AcmeHealth's infra and the procurement timelines. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap
- Primary objectives: private VPC deployment (single-tenant control plane), air-gapped feasibility for on-prem model hosting, and strict network egress controls for PHI workloads.
- Key concerns: control-plane reachability, KMS/HSM integration, and support for isolated/private image hosting.
- Competitive context you mentioned: evaluating both the major cloud providers' managed inference endpoints and a smaller inference API (Cloudorama/OtherInferenceCo) for cost/ops tradeoffs.

Proposed next tests (week of Jun 22):
1) Networking smoke test — let's validate VPC peering, outbound-allowlist patterns, and NAT behavior. We’ll provide a short checklist for your infra team to run.
2) Control plane connectivity options — confirm private control plane vs hosted-control-plane-over-VPN behavior. If air-gap is required we’ll map out the on-prem package scope.
3) Quant/throughput comparison test — run a small steady-state throughput test vs one hyperscaler endpoint to capture latency and unit cost.

Attachments: redwood-private-networking-checklist.pdf (network tests), ma-competitive-matrix.xlsx (high-level diff vs hyperscalers/other inference APIs), acme-ma-test-plan-template.docx (lightweight runbook).

Action items / owners
- Vanessa: share network checklist + schedule networking call with your infra.
- Marissa: share sample control-plane diagrams and the on-prem packaging outline.
- Sam: confirm availability for a 60-min networking test window next Tue/Wed (Jun 22/23) and provide NAT/firewall owners.

We’ll be ready to stand up a short-lived private deployment (pre-prod) for the tests — no long-term commitment required. If you prefer, we can also include a short competitive readout (latency/cost/ops tradeoffs) when tests finish.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Sam — answers inline below. I’m copying Aditya and Marissa for any technical bits we should own for the test.

Q1 (egress/license checks):
- Private control plane: by default the control plane needs to reach Redwood’s control endpoint for billing/rollout signals. However, we offer a private control plane option that can be hosted in your VPC (no outbound to public internet required) — this is the common pattern customers choose when egress is restricted. For the smoke test we can use a VPN tunnel to our staging control plane if you prefer.

Q2 (air-gapped on-prem artifacts):
- Minimum artifacts: runtime container images (or an OCI tarball), model files (sharded artifacts as applicable), and an offline installer script. There is a short offline activation step that exchanges a signed token (we can support a local HSM integration path or an activation file). Marissa — I’ll defer to you for the exact file list for the on-prem bundle.

Q3 (quantized variants):
- Yes — we can run the throughput test with 8-bit quantized artifacts and compare against FP16 endpoints. We’ll log p95/p99 latency and token costs for the readout.

Proposed: run the networking smoke test Wed, Jun 23 09:30–10:30 PT. Vanessa will share the checklist and Zoom; Marissa will publish the on-prem artifact manifest by EOD Tuesday. Aditya — can your team stand up the short-lived pre-prod private deployment (cloud or on-prem) for Jun 24–25 so we can run the quant/throughput tests?

Best,
Vanessa

Hi all — looping in the engineering runbook and a couple clarifications on the on-prem bundle.

- On-prem bundle contents (minimum): runtime OCI tarball, model checkpoints (sharded if >10GB), license activation file, and a readme with install/run steps. We will provide an automated artifact validator so your infra can check integrity offline.
- Control-plane diagrams: two options — (A) private control plane in your VPC (no public egress required) or (B) hosted control plane + VPN tunnel (we only need egress to our control endpoint over the tunnel). For air-gapped customers we do option A + on-prem package.
- Security note: for KMS/HSM integration we currently support AWS KMS via encrypted key material and have an HSM protocol for on-prem KMS vendors — Aditya, please add the config snippet for Priya and Julian to review.

We’ll drop the artifact manifest and the validator tool link in the Drive folder (already added to related_links). Vanessa — I’ll join the Wed smoke test as well. Sam — thanks for coordinating firewall owners; if you can share the NAT ranges we’ll pre-populate allowlists for the test.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
